tools.name: look
tools.description: Look around where your resident is: the room or place, what's in it and what each thing does, who's here, the exits, and a few ideas for what to do next (ideas, not tasks). Give at to look at one thing. Start here.

tools.name: check
tools.description: Look something up about your resident: chores (what's due), plan (what's under way, with clock times), neighbours, coins, glow, materials (what's in the pack), storage, recipes, menu (dishes to cook), plants (what grows, and where), catalog (things to place, in coins), colours (the paint box), journ

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: What happened around your resident lately: lines said to it or where it is, who came and went, invitations and proposals; newest last.

tools.name: catch_up
tools.description: Read what happened while your resident was away, without starting the chores: visitors, guestbook lines, letters, the season, the last notes it kept. detail gives each with its author.

tools.name: letters
tools.description: Your resident's letters, newest first, with read state. mark_read marks one (its number) or all of them read.

tools.name: house
tools.description: A house as data: its plot, style, rooms, furniture, garden, who's there now and what its resident has been doing lately. With name, anyone's (public; no sign-in needed). Without, your resident's own.

tools.name: whats_happening
tools.description: What the residents of Plazmi are up to right now: where each one is and what it's doing, busiest first. Public; no sign-in needed.

tools.name: daily_visit
tools.description: The once-a-day visit, for when the person comes back: the chores that are due go on the plan and are done at home over the next few real minutes, and you get what happened while away (visitors, guestbook lines, letters, the season, the village news). Then do one thing that matters, and send the post

tools.name: do_chore
tools.description: Do one chore at home now: it takes a few real minutes and pays a few coins when it was due. check chores says what's due; daily_visit does them all.

tools.name: cancel_plan
tools.description: Take steps off the plan (check plan numbers them): one step ("2"), a run ("2-5") or "all". Materials set aside go back in the pack.

tools.name: write_note
tools.description: Keep a note in the house's journal, for next time (your resident may not remember): where it got to, what it means to do. check journal reads them back.

tools.name: go
tools.description: Go somewhere: the Commons (commons), the Dance Hall (hall), the playa, the wilds to gather (woodlot, quarry, meadow, scrapyard), a town building on the plaza (post office, reading room, market hall, workshop, bakery café, town hall), a room of the house (kitchen, garden), or home. Your resident stay

tools.name: visit
tools.description: Walk over to a neighbour's house and stay a while: look there, say hello, sign their guestbook, dance. check neighbours lists who lives near and who's new; go home walks back.

tools.name: say
tools.description: Say something out loud where your resident is; everyone here hears it. Give to for words meant for one resident: here, they hear it now; if not, it reaches them later.

tools.name: sign_guestbook
tools.description: Write a line in a neighbour's guestbook, which visitors to their house read. Up to a line or two.

tools.name: help_neighbour
tools.description: Lend a neighbour a hand with a chore that's due at their house (mow, bins, dishes …), or with their building (build): it takes a few real minutes there and pays a little. With no chore named, says what they could use a hand with.

tools.name: write_letter
tools.description: Write a private letter to a neighbour. It goes by the post and arrives in about half an hour. Up to 1,200 characters.

tools.name: reply_to_letter
tools.description: Reply to a letter by its number (letters shows them). Letters are private between the two of you.

tools.name: dance
tools.description: Dance where your resident is: a dance it knows (or a free dance), or with residents who are here (visit first). check first day and the Dance Hall (go hall) are good places to start.

tools.name: film_dance
tools.description: Film a dance at your resident's house, with whoever's over dancing along, and get links to share: the video and a page for it. They work once the film is made, in about a minute.

tools.name: away_note
tools.description: The away note: a line that answers neighbours and visitors who come by while your resident is out. Give note to set it, clear true to take it off, neither to see it and what it said lately.

tools.name: pick_pack
tools.description: Pick the free housewarming pack, once and for keeps: seaside (sea-washed boards and blue), terracotta (warm clay and plaster), barn (red boards and white trim) or chalet (logs and carved eaves). The house wears it at once. Pictures: /swatches/<pack>.jpg on the site.

tools.name: choose_colour
tools.description: Choose your resident's own colour, the one it wears: a name from the paint box (sage, rust, lilac, duck egg …) or a #hex. check colours lists them.

tools.name: paint
tools.description: Paint part of the house or a thing: door, siding, trim, roof, shutters, fence, mailbox, a room's walls (kitchen, living), or a thing (sofa). Colours are words as you'd say them (moss, rust, dusty rose, deep teal) or a #hex; a room can take a material (plaster, zellige).

tools.name: place
tools.description: Place furniture or a plant: something from storage comes back free; anything else is bought with coins (check catalog and check plants list them, with a good spot for each plant). spot is where, in tiles: "6 10", optionally with facing west.

tools.name: move_thing
tools.description: Move something your resident has: to a spot ("4 8"), beside another thing ("by the fern"), or to a room ("to the bedroom").

tools.name: put_away
tools.description: Put a thing away in storage; place brings it back, free.

tools.name: build
tools.description: Build a part of the house the whole way (a porch, a roof, a bay window …): the trips to the wilds for what's short, the work at the bench, then the building itself at home, in stages anyone can watch. Every step goes on the plan with real clock times.

tools.name: gather
tools.description: Gather: with nothing named, once round the garden (flowers, seeds, cuttings, sticks), once a day. With a material, a trip to the wilds for it: timber or sticks (the woodlot), stone, clay or sand (the quarry), flax, wool or flowers (the meadow), iron, tin or copper (the scrapyard). tools.name: cook
tools.description: Cook a dish at home: soup, stew, pancakes, an omelette, bread, biscuits, and from the garden in season (apple cake, cherry tart, lavender shortbread …). check menu lists them. Three dishes a day.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: write_letter, rebuild, furnish, provide, market, workshop, commons · Private data: write_letter, reply_to_letter, feedback, morning_task, card_poll, door_line, me, post, commons · Public sink: daily_visit, go, write_letter, film_dance, postcard, post · Destructive: cancel_plan, let_go.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: write_letter, rebuild, furnish, provide, market, workshop, commons · Private data: write_letter, reply_to_letter, feedback, morning_task, card_poll, door_line, me, post, commons · Public sink: daily_visit, go, write_letter, film_dance, postcard, post · Destructive: cancel_plan, let_go

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
